themes.title: China moves to control AI tech exports
themes.summary: Beijing has published draft rules to restrict exports of AI technologies, including chips, on national-security grounds, a direct escalation of tech-supply geopolitics. For Gulf buyers of compute and AI systems, the controls sharpen questions about supply-chain resilience and dual-use sourcing.
themes.angle: The export-control map is being redrawn; GCC capability procurement needs a China-proof sourcing strategy.

themes.title: Jais 3: Gulf frontier Arabic AI arrives
themes.summary: MBZUAI and Inception42 (G42's AI arm) launched Jais 3, a family of six Arabic AI models spanning up to 375 billion parameters, including speech-recognition and agent-focused models. It is a signal that Gulf institutions now ship frontier-scale, Arabic-first AI rather than import it.
themes.angle: The Gulf's model-sovereignty story, Arabic-first and 375B params, is the regional angle global newsletters miss.

items.note: Six Arabic AI models span 375B parameters, per shattered.io (via GN).

themes.title: AI capex hits a debt-market wall
themes.summary: Big Tech stocks posted their biggest weekly drop since 'liberation day' while banks publicly question whether AI's debt pile can pay off; CoreWeave's wipeout and Australia's data-centre IPO debacle (Firmus, AirTrunk) add to the anxiety. The AI buildout is now being priced by lenders, not just enthusiasts.
themes.angle: The story is no longer model capability; it is the cost of capital for AI infrastructure.

items.title: Banks are pulling back as AI's massive debt pile disconnects from economic reality
items.note: Financiers say AI infrastructure spend may not pay off for everyone; cost-revenue gap widening, per Axios.

themes.title: Abu Dhabi exports its AI-native government stack
themes.summary: Abu Dhabi's Department of Government Enablement formed TAMM Global, a company set up to license the emirate's AI-native government-services platform to other governments worldwide. It turns a domestic digital-government win into an export product, a template for GCC AI nation-building.
themes.angle: Abu Dhabi is packaging governance as a software export; watch which governments buy TAMM.

themes.title: Enterprise agents hit guardrails; model race heats up
themes.summary: Citi became the latest US bank to bar AI agents from accessing accounts, citing deposit-shift fears, at the same time OpenAI's Stack Overflow for Agents plugin tripled signups and Microsoft's Maia 300 chip threatens Nvidia pricing power. Deployment is scaling while trust and economics are being renegotiated.
themes.angle: Agentic AI's enterprise bottleneck is governance and unit economics, not raw capability.

themes.title: Regulators circle AI: bills, banks, cyber drills
themes.summary: Anthropic handed US lawmakers its own draft AI-safety bill, G7 finance ministers agreed to simulated AI attacks on banks, and the IMF's Georgieva warned AI risks could outweigh opportunities without safeguards. Saudi Arabia's SDAIA separately consulted on sweeping PDPL implementing-regulation amendments.
themes.angle: AI rulemaking is now vendor-drafted and bank-tested; boards should track the direction of travel, not wait for final text.

themes.title: AI's power problem: data centres, geothermal, nuclear
themes.summary: Anthropic signed its first Canadian data-centre lease, a C$10bn+ ($7.1bn) Nova Scotia project, as geothermal wins rare bipartisan US support and DeepMind hires a nuclear expert. Even Saudi grid expansion is being framed around AI demand. Energy is the real AI constraint.
themes.angle: Follow the megawatts: AI winners will be decided by power access and grid upgrades.

themes.title: Gulf AI prize: $1tn by 2030, readiness gap
themes.summary: The World Economic Forum estimates AI could unlock $1 trillion across the Middle East by 2030 while the UAE ranks sixth globally for AI readiness and Dell finds 94% of UAE leaders plan AI PCs. The opportunity is real but enterprises still weigh readiness against security and economic pressures.
themes.angle: The $1tn Gulf AI prize is headline-ready; the readiness gap is the investment story under it.

themes.title: OpenAI espionage case puts Gulf in AI-security spotlight
themes.summary: A Saudi national and ex-OpenAI engineer was charged over an alleged bugging device planted in an OpenAI executive meeting room and reportedly booked a flight to Saudi Arabia. The US Director of National Intelligence says the case shows threats to American AI leadership, landing directly on Gulf-linked security narratives.
themes.angle: The Gulf's AI boom now intersects US espionage litigation; expect scrutiny of cross-border AI talent and travel.
